title: Rules of football (soccer)
examples: Teacher, what is the offside rule again?
Can you show us where the penalty area is?
What counts as a foul in football?

explain.say: Today we learn about the rules of football.
The pitch has a centre circle in the middle.
The offside rule stops players from just standing near the goal.
A foul happens when a player breaks the rules by tackling or pushing.
In real life, you see these rules when playing a game.
A common mistake is thinking offside only happens near the goal.

faq.q: What is the main purpose of the offside rule?
faq.a: It stops players from just waiting near the opponent's goal. It keeps the game moving and fair for everyone.
asks: Why can't I just stand near the goal?
Does the offside rule always apply?

faq.a: A foul is any illegal action, like tripping someone or pushing them. The referee will call it out.
asks: If I bump someone, is that a foul?

faq.q: What are the main parts of the pitch?
faq.a: The pitch has goal areas, a centre circle, and touchlines. These lines mark where the game can be played.
asks: What do the goal lines mark?

faq.q: Does the offside rule apply when I am passing the ball?
faq.a: The rule looks at where you are when the pass is made. You must not be too far ahead of the ball pass.
asks: Do I have to be behind the ball?
When does the offside rule check my position?

faq.q: Are there different types of fouls?
faq.a: Yes, some fouls are minor, and some are more serious. The referee decides the punishment.
asks: What is the difference between a foul and a warning?
Can a foul result in a penalty kick?

facts: The pitch has marked areas like the penalty area.
The offside rule prevents players from gaining an unfair advantage.
A foul is any breach of the game's rules by a player.
The centre circle is used for kick-offs at the start of play.

quiz.say: A player is standing near the opponent's goal waiting for a pass.

options.show: It only matters if the ball is kicked.
options.say: It only matters if the ball is kicked.

options.show: The referee will never see it.
options.say: The referee will never see it.

options.show: It is always okay to stand there.
options.say: It is always okay to stand there.

quiz.why: The offside rule is designed to prevent players from waiting illegally near the goal.

wrong.0: This is wrong because your position matters even before the ball is kicked.
wrong.1: This is wrong because referees are trained to spot these rule breaks.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the rule exists for a reason to keep the game fair.

quiz.say: If a player trips an opponent, what has happened?

options.show: It is just part of the game.
options.say: It is just part of the game.

quiz.why: Tripping someone is a clear example of illegal physical contact, which is a foul.

wrong.0: This is wrong because tripping is usually considered a more serious foul.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the player who caused the fall is responsible for the foul.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the rules define what is acceptable physical contact.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of the centre circle?

options.show: It is where penalties are scored.
options.say: It is where penalties are scored.

options.show: It is the area for corner kicks.
options.say: It is the area for corner kicks.

options.show: It is just a decorative line.
options.say: It is just a decorative line.

quiz.why: The centre circle is the designated spot for the kick-off when play begins.

wrong.0: This is wrong because penalties are scored from the penalty spot, not the centre circle.
wrong.1: This is wrong because corner kicks happen near the goal line.
wrong.2: This is wrong because it has a specific role in starting the match.
